title: CAEHR – Cardiovascular Diseases – Enhancing Healthcare through cross-Sectoral Routine data integration: Use Case Emergency
summary:
CAEHR is a research project that demonstrates how improved digital connectivity in healthcare can enhance medical care. Using cardiovascular diseases as an example, the project investigates how medical information can be captured and utilized consistently across the entire continuum of care in order to make treatment faster, more targeted, and more effective.

A particular focus is placed on the emergency care of patients with stroke. Building on successful approaches from the first project phase, digital communication pathways between emergency medical services and stroke centers will be further developed and transferred to additional sites (UMG, MHH, and Vivantes). The objective is to ensure the reliable availability of relevant medical information even before hospital admission.

Specifically, data availability will be expanded through the exchange of patients’ medication information via the electronic patient record, prehospital vital-sign data, continuously recorded electrocardiogram (ECG) data as captured in the ambulance, and the standardized emergency care report. Early access to this information is expected to facilitate better preparation of in-hospital treatment and enable earlier initiation of care, particularly in time-critical emergencies such as stroke.
conditions: Patients with suspected ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, or transient ischemic attack (TIA). As no ICD-10 codes are available for the pre-hospital setting, the target population can be determined on the basis of the standardised national patient referral codes (PCZ via IVENA) using the corresponding referral codes 421, 423 and 425.

interventions.name: Prospective data collection to evaluate the quality of stroke care before, during, and after the implementation, expansion, and optimization of interfaces between the prehospital and hospital sectors at participating sites, including a standardized 3-month follow-up survey.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
● Suspected acute stroke (i.e., cerebral ischemia, subarachnoid hemorrhage, or intracerebral hemorrhage) or transient ischemic attack (TIA), with subsequent inpatient treatment
● Written informed consent for study participation provided by the patient or their legal representative
● Presentation to or admission at the participating study site via emergency medical services (EMS)
Exclusion criteria:
● Age < 18 years
